summary: Conche Light, at the entrance to Conche Harbour on the Great Northern Peninsula: a square wooden tower of 1914, with the working light moved to a skeleton tower in 1992.

structures.note: Still standing; owned and maintained by the Town of Conche (Lighthouse Friends). Converted to battery power in 1977. No longer the working light after 1992.

structures.type: square skeleton tower with red and white daymark
structures.note: Erected by the Canadian Coast Guard farther out on the reef, in aluminium frame (Lighthouse Friends); listed as Conche Light in the Coast Guard list.

corrections.why: The Coast Guard list gives Conche Light (H0722) at 50 53 09.9 N, 055 53 50.2 W. The record's longitude, 055 53 40.9 W, is the position of the Conche Wharf Light (H0723) in the same list.
Lighthouse Friends says the wooden lighthouse is owned by the Town of Conche. The record, from Rowlett's directory, says Village. A human should check which name the municipality uses.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources differed on whether the light is still lit. The wooden tower of 1914 stopped being the working light when the Coast Guard erected a new tower farther out in 1992 (Lighthouse Friends). The Coast Guard list still shows Conche Light, a red light flashing every five seconds, so the light continues from the 1992 tower; the list marks it seasonal.
The record's 1992 'deactivated' event belongs to the wooden tower. The light continued from the 1992 tower.

notes_for_editor: Thin station: two sources, both read in full, a Lighthouse Friends page and the Coast Guard list. The record's location longitude is the wharf light's, not Conche Light's (see corrections). Lighthouse Friends says the wooden tower 'remains standing today' and also says the 1992 tower replaced it; the story reads both as the old tower standing and no longer working. Keepers: Lighthouse Friends gives Matthew McGrath 'at least 1939' and Cyril Clements with no years. The Lighthouse Digest database names Clements as caretaker, but that page returned an error when checked, so the word is not used. The Wikipedia Conche article (leads only, not cited) gives the 1992 tower a 6-second flash and calls the managing agent Village of Conche. The Coast Guard list gives 5 seconds, used here. No storm, wreck or rescue at the station was found; the 1860 Dower rescue predates the light and is not tied to it in any source. Not verified on the ground. Revised 2026-10-28 by the fact-checker: the story now says the Coast Guard list marks Conche Light seasonal; two sentences that followed Lighthouse Friends' wording closely were rewritten; two sentences missing footnotes were footnoted to Lighthouse Friends.
